Compute the fraction of available light (light) for each cohort based on the given parameters

Source: R/Processes.R
competition.Rd

This function calculates the fraction of available light for each cohort of trees based on their diameter at breast height (dbh), species, number of trees, and global parameters.

Usage

competition(
  dbh,
  species,
  trees,
  parComp,
  h = NULL,
  patch_size_ha,
  ba = NULL,
  cohortHeights = NULL,
  n_quantiles = 10,
  continuous = FALSE,
  light_mask = TRUE
)

Arguments

dbh

torch.Tensor Diameter at breast height for each cohort, in cm, [sites, patches, cohorts].

species

torch.Tensor (int64) species index for each cohort, [sites, patches, cohorts].

trees

torch.Tensor Number of trees in each cohort, [sites, patches, cohorts].

parComp

torch.Tensor Competition parameters, one row per species and two columns: the height parameter of height() and the competition strength.

h

(Optional) Defaults to NULL: the light each cohort receives at its own height. Any non-NULL value returns the light at the forest floor instead, one value per patch ([sites, patches, 1]), which is what the regeneration process is given; the value itself is not used.

patch_size_ha

numeric Patch size in hectares.

ba

torch.Tensor (Optional) Pre-computed basal area. Defaults to NULL.

cohortHeights

torch.Tensor (Optional) Pre-computed cohort heights. Defaults to NULL.

n_quantiles

integer Number of height quantiles used when continuous = FALSE. Defaults to 10.

continuous

logical Use the continuous competition formulation. Defaults to FALSE.

light_mask

logical Take the height quantiles over the live cohorts only (trees > 0.5), leaving every cohort's real height as the bin query. Defaults to TRUE since 0.2.0: unmasked, the padded cohort width is set by the widest site in the batch, so the same stand's light depends on which other sites happen to share its batch. FALSE reproduces earlier results. See createProcess() for the measurement.

Value

torch.Tensor Fraction of available light (between 0 and 1) for each cohort, [sites, patches, cohorts]; with h given, the light at the forest floor, [sites, patches, 1].

Details

The light of a cohort is one minus the weighted basal area of the cohorts of its patch that are taller than it (by more than 0.1 m), light = max(0, 1 - sum(BA_taller * parComp[, 2] * 0.1)), where BA is the basal area in m^2/ha (BA_stand()) and the height comes from height() with the species' height parameter parComp[, 1]. With a competition strength of 0.2 (about the start value) a cohort under 50 m^2/ha of taller trees receives no light. In a model the function is the competition process, createProcess(func = competition); it takes no environment.

See also

height(), BA_stand(), createProcess() (n_quantiles, continuous, light_mask), finn()

Examples

# the light of three cohorts on one 0.1 ha patch: two 50-cm trees, ten 20-cm
# trees and forty 5-cm trees of one species (height parameter 0.5,
# competition strength 0.2)
shape   <- c(1, 1, 3)
dbh     <- torch::torch_tensor(array(c(50, 20, 5), shape))
trees   <- torch::torch_tensor(array(c(2, 10, 40), shape))
species <- torch::torch_tensor(array(1L, shape), dtype = torch::torch_long())
parComp <- torch::torch_tensor(matrix(c(0.5, 0.2), nrow = 1))
# the tallest cohort is in full light, each smaller one is shaded by the
# basal area above it
competition(dbh, species, trees, parComp, patch_size_ha = 0.1, continuous = TRUE)
#> torch_tensor
#> (1,.,.) = 
#>   1.0000  0.9215  0.8586
#> [ CPUFloatType{1,1,3} ]
# the light that reaches the forest floor, where the recruits start
competition(dbh, species, trees, parComp, h = 0, patch_size_ha = 0.1)
#> torch_tensor
#> (1,.,.) = 
#>   0.8429
#> [ CPUFloatType{1,1,1} ]

# the light model as the competition process of a model. It takes no
# environment; `continuous = TRUE` compares every pair of cohorts instead of
# binning them into height quantiles
m <- finn(N_species = 2,
          competition_process = createProcess(func = competition, continuous = TRUE))

# a 30-year simulation from bare ground; an unfitted model uses `env` as
# given (no scaling constants yet), so the predictor is passed standardised
env <- data.frame(siteID = 1L, year = 1:30, temp = 0)
sim <- simulateForest(m, env = env, patches = 5, patch_size = 0.1)
tail(sim$wide$site)
